craft_notes: Sthāyin: parāmarśa-śakti unit 27 — jñāna-viśrānti of doctrine-reveal (owner reviews first-verse of chapter). Sanskrit-first: bīja-vowels held letter-exact (a i u / ā ī ū / e oṃ / ai au / e ai o au / am / aḥ); ra/la, varga-names (ka ca ṭa ta pa), and Śrīkālikā kept as terms. Rows: 2 (compound-lists kept whole), 6 (gait of refutation: na … api … ca), 9 (end-weight doctrine words line-final), 1 (colon-lands before catalogs). Close: verdicts line-final. Rejected: smoothing the sixteen-bīja arithmetic — killed: the count IS the doctrine; anglicizing letter-names (ka-class → 'k-row') — killed: the Sanskrit names stand. Read aloud: cadence-checked — each seed and count lands on stress. Divided/undivided dyad: power-endowed and power both kept.

lines: When contemplation is by undividedness alone,
the Lord is one as the seed-womb — divided in part,
l4.sanskrit_cite: ity evam iyato yadā nirvibhāgatayā eva parāmarśaḥ tadā eka eva bhagavān bījayonitayā bhāgaśaḥ parāmarśe śaktimān śaktiś ca

reads_against.argmap: What happens when parāmarśa is undivided? → Undivided = ekatva of Lord and śakti; divided = the śaktimān/śakti dyad — the bīja-yoni keeps both readings.
c1_essence: Undivided contemplation collapses Lord and power into the one seed-womb; divided, the power-endowed/power dyad stands.
reads_against.c1_rasa: śānta with vimarśa weight (rest carrying the letter-scheme)
